payload.title: Who produces a Goal's /goal prompt?
payload.body: Scenarios that separate the rivals: (a) the same log read twice gives the same bytes; (b) a Goal whose body has no valid constraints block gets no prompt and a refusal; (c) in a store with two Goals, only the asked Goal's items appear.

why: Contested design question of issue #113; the owner settled it in session 2026-11-12.

payload.title: A hyp command prints the prompt from the log
payload.body: hyp prompt <G-id> --actor <A> reads the log and prints the prompt, so scenarios (a), (b) and (c) are checked by go test.

why: Rival 1, the owner's choice in session 2026-11-12.

payload.title: The grill skill writes the prompt from hyp show and hyp status
payload.body: The grill skill composes the prompt as prose each session; no command reads the log for it.

why: Rival 2, the alternative the issue left open.

payload.title: Session decision on who produces the prompt
payload.body: Rule, fixed before the record: the owner settled this question in the session of 2026-11-12, so this Experiment is an argument, not a run. H-BM50HC supports when a command that reads the log can meet scenarios (a), (b) and (c) of the question. H-QZMAYS contradicts when prose written per session cannot guarantee (a) or (b): two sessions can word it differently (a), and no exit code can refuse a Goal with no block (b). Evidence: scenarios.md in this Experiment's evidence directory.

why: Records the owner's settlement of Q-PZ1M37 with the session as evidence.

payload.observation: Session decision, recorded under the pre-registered rule: scenarios (a), (b) and (c) favour a command that reads the log; the owner settled it on 2026-11-12.
